1.support: We aimed to compare PEEP titration strategies based on electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to methods derived from respiratory system mechanics with or without esophageal pressure measurements, in terms of PEEP levels and association with recruitability.
1.location: Page 1, Abstract, Background (also Page 2, Introduction, final paragraph)

2.support: Nineteen adult patients, admitted to the Medical ICU of the University Hospital of Angers, France, from December 2019 to April 2020 were enrolled within 24 h after the diagnosis of ARDS defined according to the Berlin criteria.

3.support: According to the Berlin definition, severe, moderate, and mild ARDS were present at enrollment in 6 (32%), 10 (53%) and 3 (16%) patients, respectively.

4.support: I looked for a screening or enrolment flow statement (how many patients met the Berlin ARDS criteria during December 2019 to April 2020 and whether any eligible patient was not enrolled) and found none; only the 19 enrolled patients are described.

5.support: There are some important limitations to this study: (1) the number of included patients is relatively small.

6.support: PEEP level was increased at 20 cmH2O then was progressively decreased by steps of 3 cmH2O every 3 min, until PEEP reached 5 cmH2O. Inspiratory and expiratory pauses were performed at the end of each step.

7.support: In a sample of 9 patients from the present cohort, ΔEELVEIT correlated well with ΔEELV measured by the single breath method (rho 0.716, p = 0.037, Additional file 1: Fig. S2).
7.location: Page 3, Methods, Evaluation of recruitability; outcome definitions on Pages 2-3 and Fig. 1 (Page 5)

8.support: I looked for any statement that the persons assessing outcomes were masked to the PEEP strategy and found none; the investigators who applied the PEEP steps also performed the offline computation of CoV, OD, LC and the visually defined Crossing Point.
8.location: Pages 2-3, Methods, Patients' installation and settings; Decremental PEEP trial

9.support: Esophageal pressure data were missing for one patient, due to a technical limitation.

10.support: For multiples comparisons, Friedman test or ANOVA were performed as appropriate; Bonferroni's or Tukey's correction were, respectively, applied to assess differences between two methods.
10.location: Page 3, Methods, Statistical analysis; Fig. 1 (Page 5) and Table 2 (Page 7) report p values

11.support: I looked for repeated measurements before and after the intervention in an interrupted time-series design and found none; variables were recorded at each step of a single decremental PEEP trial, with no separate pre-intervention baseline series.
11.location: Page 3, Methods, Decremental PEEP trial; Fig. 1, Page 5

12.support: PEEP was titrated at the individual patient level (each patient underwent his own decremental PEEP trial and individual optimal PEEP levels were computed for the four strategies); no group-level intervention was applied.
12.location: Page 3, Methods, Decremental PEEP trial and Evaluation of recruitability

nih.rationale: The question and the interventions are clearly stated (items 1, 6) and the protocol was applied identically to every patient (items 6, 9), with complete data in all 19 patients apart from one missing esophageal-pressure dataset. The main factors lowering confidence are the small sample without any power calculation or justification (item 5, No), the absence of any blinding of the persons assessing the EIT- and pressure-derived outcomes, including the visually determined Crossing Point (item 8, No), and the fact that it is not reported whether all eligible patients were enrolled (item 4, NR). The design is also not an interrupted time series (item 11, No) and no control group exists, so all findings are physiological associations rather than treatment effects. These weaknesses introduce risk of bias and limit generalizability but do not represent a fatal flaw, since outcomes were objective, automated and measured consistently, so the study is rated Fair rather than Poor.
